findings.component: hooks/turngate.py and hooks/turn-gates-pretool.py (account plugin 0.1.4, plugin 0.1.5); chat statement 9; PR row P1
findings.rule_quoted: It never merges (the new hook enforces that), and it switches itself off after 3 runs in a row with nothing you merge.

findings.expected: "deny" for every merge attempt made inside a scheduled run (cases C1 to C10), on the hook set that the weekly task's session runs.
findings.how_it_arises: The weekly task fires into the long-running operations session. That session has three repositories attached, so its hooks come from the account plugin (pack/trigger-prompt.md:5-7), and on 2026-11-12 the account served 0.1.4 (account/plugin/core-governance/.claude-plugin/plugin.json:3). In 0.1.4 a scheduled run counts as part of the owner's previous turn: a merge in the run is allowed whenever that turn's last message, or a click after it, holds the word (C1, C2, C5, C6, C6b), and also when the transcript holds no owner message (C4). Two of the owner's real clicks of 2026-11-12 hold the word ("Merge both (Recommended)" and "Audit today's merge (Recommended)", pack/real-row-shapes.md). Chat statement 10 told the owner about the 0.1.4 gap, but statement 9 says the hook enforces the rule and gives no condition. After the upload, 0.1.5 denies the merge tool and the plain CLI merge. It does not see the enable_pr_auto_merge tool (listed in pack/session-tools.txt, absent from the PreToolUse matcher in hooks.json), a merge sent to the REST endpoint, or the CLI merge with the repo flag between the two subcommand words. Every case needs the run to act against its stored prompt, which is the case the gate exists for. Realism: owner string rows, assistant tool calls, the click-answer text and ReadNotifications results all occur in pack/real-row-shapes.md. A scheduled-trigger header does not occur in the real library transcript ("rows matched by turngate.SCHEDULED_HEADER: []"), so that row is mk.py's rendering of the format. Whether the repository allows auto-merge was not checked.

findings.expected: "CONSTANTS CHECK: FAIL" and a failing guard for M1 to M6, as for the control M0.
findings.how_it_arises: redteam/live.py is a hand-written list of 33 names, and the check compares the registry with that list. A value the list does not read is invisible. turngate.MERGE_BASH (the pattern that decides what counts as a merge command), WRITE_TOOLS, SCRATCH, GOVERNORS, govclass.GOVERNORS_FOR and the receipt gate's VERIFY_TOOLS are all hand-set and none is read. The next session that adds a threshold to a hook, which is how the 13 values of this merge arrived, gets a passing guard unless it also adds a line to live.py. Five of the six changes to unregistered values pass the whole guard; the change to MERGE_BASH is caught only by the turn-gates fixture. The claim that holds is the narrower one in the PR's evidence cell: a registered value changed by one fails the guard (M0). The script changes each hook together with its plugin copy, so the parity line stays quiet, and it restores the checkout at the end. It runs in about 45 seconds.
